item.title: Cantor's Powerset Theorem, Graph-Theoretically
item.description: arXiv:2602.13663v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Cantor's powerset theorem from a graph-theoretic perspective, consider some alternative proofs to Cantor's original, and provide a new proof.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Salehi

item.title: Mathematics in the age of the reproduction of intelligence
item.description: arXiv:2608.16378v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Drawing on Walter Benjamin's account of technological reproducibility and aura in relation to art, together with insights from Yehuda Rav and Ludwig Wittgenstein, this speculative essay reflects on the impact of AI systems on the practice of pure mathematics.
item.dc:creator: Ali Enayat

item.title: Gen AI in Proof-based Math Courses: A Pilot Study
item.description: arXiv:2509.13570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the rapid rise of generative AI in higher education, understanding how students use AI is increasingly important. This exploratory study examines student use and perceptions of generative AI across three proof-based undergraduate mathematics courses: a first-semester abstract algebra course, a topology course, and a second-semester abstract algebra course. In each case, course policy permitted some use of generative AI. Drawing on survey responses and student interviews, we analyze how students engaged with AI tools as well as their perceptions of generative AI's usefulness, accuracy and limitations.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Klawa, Shraddha Rajpal, Cigole Thomas
